The authors consider point transformed electromagnetic invisibility cloaks in transformation media obtained by transformation from general anisotropic media.
The cloaked object is completely decoupled from the exterior.
The solutions of Maxwell's equations are discontinuous at the boundary of the cloaked object.
The transformation matrix Aλ determines the transformation of the electromagnetic fields under the transformation of the coordinates.
The determinant of the transformation matrix Aλ is equal to ∆(y) = g′(y c) gj(|y−cj|).
The electric and magnetic fields transform as E λ(x) = Aλ λ′ (y)E 0,λ′(y) and H λ(x) = Aλ λ′ (y)H 0,λ′(y).
The magnetic induction and electric displacement transform as Bλ(x) = (∆(y))−1Aλ (y)Bλ′ (y) and Dλ(x) = (∆(y))−1Aλ (y)Dλ′ (y).
The permittivity and permeability transform as ελν(x) = (∆(y))−1Aλ (y)Aν (y)ελ′ν′ (y).
The authors propose a method to enhance cloaking in approximate transformation media by coating the boundary of the cloaked object with a material that imposes the boundary conditions.
The cloaking boundary conditions determine whether the cloaking effect is achieved or not.
The normal components of the curl of the electric and magnetic fields have to vanish at the inside of the boundary of the cloaked object.
The tangential components of the electric and magnetic fields have to vanish at the outside of the boundary of the cloaked object.
